title: Who Authorizes a Nested Call?
description: Contract A calls contract B, and B calls `player.require_auth()`. The player signed only the transaction that invokes A. Select the statement that correctly describes how Soroban resolves the requirement.

content.prompt: A player submits one transaction that invokes contract A. A cross-contract call invokes contract B, and B executes `player.require_auth()`. Which statement is true?
options: No player authorization is needed because B is reached through A rather than the transaction root.
The player must have authorized an invocation entry covering the call path to B, either directly or through a sub-invocation entry.
`require_auth` inside a nested call is ignored unless B is the transaction's root contract.
Only the contract address of A can satisfy the player's authorization entry.

solution: The player must have authorized an invocation entry covering the call path to B, either directly or through a sub-invocation entry.
hint: Authorization is evaluated against the whole invocation tree, not just the transaction's root contract. A root-level authorization may be reused only when the required invocation is part of that authorized subtree; otherwise the signer must include a sub-invocation entry that matches the nested call, its contract, and its arguments. Contract addresses do not inherit a player's signature.
author: StellarHunts Core

testCases.title: Contract address cannot sign for the player
